top_signal.title: IP Revival for 1980s Toy Brand. Advice Needed
top_signal.summary: Hello, everyone.   I own a company called Select Merchandise.   Founded in 1982, Select Merchandise brought affordable toys to store shelves across the country. Its best-known product was Convertors, a transforming robot line that competed with Transformers and GoBots during the 1980s.   For the past two years, I've been working to bring Select and Convertors back. I've spent that time researching the company's history, rebuilding its identity, establishing a new LLC, filing trademarks, developing a website and publishing strategy, contacting industry professionals, and putting together a substantial business plan.   My goal is to revive Convertors through comics and publishing before eventually returning to robot manufacturing. I have several projects planned, and I'm now at the point where I need to hire artists, writers, and editors to get the first product into production.   Unfortunately, financing has become my biggest obstacle.   For anyone who's launched an independent comic publisher, revived an older entertainment property, or raised capital for a small IP-based business: How did you finance your first commercial release? Were there particular organizations, investors, or partnerships that helped you get started?   I also have a second question: How do you get people to respond to emails and phone calls?
